name: Official TypeSafe skill

name: TypeSafe Python SDK
description: Official Python client, with a support-ticket routing example.

name: TypeSafe JavaScript SDK
description: Official JavaScript and TypeScript client.

name: Jevify
description: Agent skill for finding places to use Jev and planning comparisons with existing code.
notes: Independent skill, not the model or an official SDK.

name: Jev Logs
description: Scores log entries with Jev to decide which need a closer look.

name: Skillbox
description: Self-hosted skill library with optional Jev-based recommendations.
notes: Jev is an optional recommender, not required for the core library.

name: Jev Ultrafast
description: Jev picks browser actions and page elements; a separate model writes text.
notes: Published timing is a narrow author-run demonstration, not a general reliability guarantee.

name: Foreman
description: Uses Jev to check a coding agent's progress and decide when it needs intervention.
notes: Architectural experiment; its README provides an offline deterministic demo.

name: Jev MCP
description: MCP tools for checking claims against evidence, screening content, and ranking candidates.
notes: Review tool permissions and environment handling before installation.

name: TypeSafe MCP
description: Go MCP server for making Jev requests from coding agents.

name: Home Assistant Jev
description: Adds Jev decisions to Home Assistant entities and automations.
notes: Inspect the example automations and keep consequential actions behind explicit policy.

name: Jev Plays Snake
description: Snake where code finds legal moves and Jev picks a direction.
notes: Useful separation of legal-action generation, model choice, deadlines, and local execution.

name: JevPilot
description: Driving simulation where Jev chooses steering and speed. Not a real-world driving system.
notes: Simulation only; not an autonomous-driving safety system. The hosted demo may require login.

name: TypeSafe Mario
description: Jev picks controller inputs from emulator state. Requires a lawful local game setup.
notes: Requires a lawful local game setup; repository does not include Nintendo ROMs.

name: PROMPT FPS / Jev Doom
description: Jev chooses actions in a browser-based Doom engine. Uses Freedoom assets.
notes: Ships Freedoom, not commercial Doom assets. Engine and content have separate GPL/BSD notices; inspect licenses/.

name: Jev Music Playground
description: Jev picks musical parameters; code turns them into notes and MIDI. Includes an offline mode.
notes: Includes an explicitly labeled offline heuristic mode; Jev does not directly generate audio.

name: OpenJev SGLang
description: Independent typed-decision server using open models and SGLang. Not official Jev weights.
notes: Not official Jev weights; no requests go to TypeSafe. Review deployment authentication and GPU costs.

name: JevAI for XMage
description: Magic: The Gathering bots that use Jev alone or alongside XMage search.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21; a plugin inside an XMage fork. The reported 11-6-3 result is the hybrid across 20 author-run games with turn-cap draws, not our reproduction. Hybrid pruning is off by default. Review server-side keys, game assets, and licenses separately.

name: Jev Chess
description: A shared chess game against Jev with move probabilities. Hosted demo; source code not verified.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Public project-page metadata inspected, not server code. No public source repository or code license verified. No shared game move was submitted, and advertised results were not reproduced.

name: tisco
description: Searches video transcripts with Jev, then previews clip moves and renames for approval.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Transcript-based, not visual video understanding. Approved transcription uploads extracted audio; requests and transcript context reach OpenRouter. Documents a synthetic offline demo, paid live calls, and preview/undo controls. No clips or credentials were supplied for this review.

name: Vibe Domain
description: Ranks domain names by the requested style. Has a no-key heuristic mode and a hosted Jev option.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Public page reviewed; no public source repository or code license verified. Documentation distinguishes a no-key heuristic mode from live OpenRouter inference. No availability check or API call was run here. Recheck names at a registrar and review key handling before entering credentials.

name: Spliit Cloud
description: Optional Jev Choice suggestions for expense categories after local dictionary and group-history matching; code interprets confidence before presenting results.
notes: Submitted by the Spliit Cloud maintainer. Hosted Jev is optional and uses a server-side key; expense titles, language, group metadata and category examples reach the configured provider, with additional expense context for bulk review. Use data approved for hosted processing and a trusted HTTPS endpoint. The custom-URL guard has a broad 127. hostname-prefix exception and requests follow redirects; this is not an end-to-end transport guarantee. Confidence and probability checks support advisory suggestions, not guaranteed categorization accuracy. Source and tests were inspected, not executed; the hosted engine was not verified and no paid inference was run. See docs/MAINTENANCE.md for the scoped review and source links.

name: jev_search
description: Ranks files by keyword, then checks their passages with Jev in two passes. Author marks it experimental.
notes: OpenRouter community winner, announced 2026-09-21. Current README attributes file prioritization to keyword-density code, not Jev. The author marks the project fully AI-generated and not for production. Source text is sent through OpenRouter; inspect privacy and spending limits and prefer environment-based credentials. No code was executed.

name: Cua Driver + jev-use
description: Cua Driver example in Python and TypeScript: Jev chooses an action, the driver runs it, and code checks the result.
notes: Cua-maintained public-preview Python/TypeScript recipe, not a Jev model built into Driver. The mock path uses no Jev credentials but still operates a browser fixture. Live choices use hosted TypeSafe; screenshots are not sent to Jev by this adapter. Driver permissions, capture freshness, and independent postconditions remain application responsibilities. October 8 recheck inspected the Python adapter, fixture runner and fake-client tests. The original September 17 X thread includes a 2048 run; the current browser-form fixture is a separate example and does not reproduce that recording.

name: Jev Cua (Codex/Waku)
description: Mac automation using Cua Driver, with optional Jev recommendations for saved workflows.
notes: Local runtime is not local Jev inference: the optional router sends best-effort-redacted requests and workflow descriptions to TypeSafe. Current README pins a specific Cua Driver version; review it before installing. Visual observations can disclose window contents to the connected client/model. Source-reviewed, not executed or security-audited.

name: jev-bot (@compootor)
description: Native Mac controls through a JavaScript MCP session, with optional Jev element selection.
notes: The @compootor/jev-bot package is distinct from unrelated repositories named jev-bot. Cua Driver is installed separately and requires desktop permissions. Direct element actions need no TypeSafe key; Jev actions do. The inspected version documents no browser-tab, coordinate-click, drag, scroll, clipboard, launch, or hotkey support. Persistent JavaScript is not a security sandbox.

name: Browser Harness (supporting driver)
description: The CDP browser connection used by Jev Ultrafast. Model-neutral, not a Jev model.
notes: Supporting infrastructure, not a Jev model or a claim that every Browser Harness task uses Jev. The dependency is declared in browser-use/jev-ultrafast/pyproject.toml. Remote debugging can expose a logged-in browser; use an isolated profile and review recording and permission settings.

name: TypeSafe computer use (macOS)
description: Mac automation using local OCR and accessibility data, with Jev choosing the next action.
notes: Requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions. Selected screen text enters model requests. Dry-run and explicit --act behavior are documented. Author cost/speed measurements were not reproduced. Previously indexed and featured in the X gallery; now also an editorial catalog selection.

name: Jev voice browser
description: Voice-controlled Playwright browser. Jev chooses actions from partial speech and page controls.
notes: A headed Chromium/Playwright application, not a native desktop driver. Uses a persistent browser profile and a loopback control server. Keep the control port private; speech processing and model requests can disclose content. Published timings are author-reported.

name: Jev Browser Skill
description: Small browser-control reference showing how to build and execute Jev action choices.
notes: A deliberately limited browser-control reference, not a general-purpose desktop driver. The source links a recorded walkthrough and explains the action loop. Inspect credential handling and permissions before installation; no live walkthrough was run here.

name: Jev Browser (MCP, CLI, library)
description: Playwright browser controlled by Jev, available as an MCP server, CLI, or library.
notes: Uses its own Playwright Chromium; installation may download a browser. Live actions need TypeSafe access, and text entry can use another provider. An early browser implementation, not a universal computer-use backend. Do not treat published demonstrations as independently reproduced.

name: Jev Browser Use (existing Codex connection)
description: Skill that uses an existing Codex browser connection. Jev clicks and scrolls; Codex types and checks the result.
notes: Reuses an existing browser connection; it does not install a new driver. The inspected README says browser execution currently requires Codex Computer Use; installability in another client does not prove execution support. Choose the skill or plugin to avoid duplicate instructions. Speed claims are workflow-specific author measurements.

name: Jev Social
description: Read-only Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn research loop: Jev Choice questions pick the platform and each bounded search, read, inspect, or finish operation; socai CLI executes in the user's Chrome and the app retains source-linked evidence.
notes: Maintainer submission. Requires OpenRouter Jev access, the socai CLI, and a logged-in Chrome session. Captured page, post, and comment text can enter Jev/OpenRouter requests; the app excludes raw DOM, tokens, cookies, headers, and local paths from public evidence. Actions are rebuilt from supported CLI capabilities and validated social URLs; TikTok media download appears only after explicit user intent. Source review covered routing, bounded action construction, target validation, evidence redaction, and project tests and documentation; this catalog did not run the application or paid inference. The recorded 64-second report is one dated local observation, not a benchmark.

name: Jevlike (independent option scorer)
description: Independent one-pass option scorer with training code and game examples. Not TypeSafe Jev.
notes: Not TypeSafe Jev weights or its unpublished architecture. Similar input/output shape does not establish equal quality. Selected game-video windows are not typical-play evidence; review checkpoint formats, model/data licenses, and evaluation controls before reuse.

name: CUA-S1-FORMS (independent specialist)
description: Cua's independent form-filling model and dataset. Not a general desktop agent or official Jev weights.
notes: Model and dataset Hub metadata were inspected; no weights were downloaded or inference run. The paired dataset is cua-ai/cua-s1-forms on Hugging Face. The GitHub component README describes a source-only research profile; do not equate that statement with absence of the separately published Hub artifact. Check exact artifact/model-card terms and task scope; no numerical performance claim is reproduced here.

name: llm-typesafe
description: Use Jev from the LLM command line or Python, with stdin, templates, and sync/async calls.
notes: Suggested by the author in issue #2. Reviewed the client and error tests, including redirect refusal and malformed JSON handling; no upstream tests or live inference were run here. Sends input to TypeSafe. The host LLM tool's normal logging can retain prompts and provider responses.

name: wellposed
description: Offline linter and agent skill for Jev requests: checks missing options, broken state references, and question types.
notes: Submitted in HN comment 49803528. Structural rules and tests were inspected, not executed. Structural lint is offline; --semantic makes paid TypeSafe calls and can send request state. Rules are heuristic and version-specific. The author's evaluation corpus is model-generated/labeled, so its reported scores are not independent validation.

name: nospace
description: Adds spaces while you type. Jev chooses between possible word splits; a separate model handles spelling corrections.
notes: Submitted in HN comment 49802812. Reviewed the provider code and tests for stale replies, caret preservation, undo, and composition input; no upstream tests or live model calls were run. English-only experimental demo; HN users reported ambiguous splits. Text reaches hosted inference through server routes, and spelling correction uses a separate paid model. Word list retains its MIT notice.

name: jevrs
description: Async Rust client with typed answers, derive macros, and native or WASI transports.
notes: Author submission in issue #4. Source review covered request framing, credential-redacted Debug, typed response/probability validation, retry tests, and native/WASI example source; no Rust build, WASI runtime, upstream test suite, or live API call was run. Unofficial client. Live inputs go to TypeSafe by default. Custom base URLs are caller-controlled and checked for URI syntax, not mandatory HTTPS: keep real credentials on trusted HTTPS endpoints. Configure transport timeouts and retry budgets. The X link was supplied by the author, not independently inspected in this pass.

name: jev-belay
description: Claude Code Stop hook that checks local run evidence before Jev judges an unverified completion claim.
notes: Submitted in PR #1. Local code establishes file-change/check evidence and fails open on errors; only redacted task/final-message text and derived counts are intended for inference. Author AUROC/latency/cost figures come from one author's model-labeled corpus and were not reproduced. Default inference is TypeSafe HTTPS; a custom JEV_BASE_URL is not forced to HTTPS, so use only trusted HTTPS endpoints with real credentials. Source-reviewed only; the hook and its upstream tests were not executed here.

name: jev-plays-pokemon-red
description: Pokemon Red agent where code builds legal actions and route state; Jev chooses only at branch points.
notes: Submitted in PR #1. Requires a lawful local Pokemon Red dump; the repository does not ship ROM or save-state game data. Unknown or failed model choices fall back to code-owned legal actions. Author timing/cost and cartridge behavior were not reproduced. Default inference is TypeSafe HTTPS; a custom JEV_BASE_URL should be a trusted HTTPS endpoint when a real bearer key is used. Source-reviewed only; no ROM, upstream tests, or live inference were run here.

name: jgrep (npm: jevgrep)
description: Jev answers one Noul per code chunk, diff hunk, or CSV row (does this match the description?); code prints the probabilities as file:line hits, gates CI on an English rule with --diff, and lists the test files a diff can affect with --tests.
notes: Every searched chunk is sent to TypeSafe; TypeSafe endpoint only. Maintainer submission.

name: Oko
description: Code-search CLI and MCP server that finds candidates locally and uses Jev to rank the source snippets.
notes: Discovered through shipwithjev.com. Reviewed ranking/transport code and local-fake HTTP test source, including finite probability checks and bounded candidate payloads; no upstream build, tests, or live inference were run. --no-jev keeps keyword ranking local; Jev ranking sends selected source text and the query to TypeSafe. Inspect setup changes to agent/project configuration before installation. Custom TYPESAFE_BASE_URL is caller-controlled: use trusted HTTPS with real keys. Author retrieval and speed benchmarks were not reproduced.

name: Tenbin
description: MCP server and skill for linting Jev questions, evaluating labeled examples, and choosing decision thresholds.
notes: Discovered through shipwithjev.com. Read the skill, SDK gateway, and ranking/batch-budget test source; no installation, upstream tests, or paid calls were run. Design and lint work offline; evaluation sends supplied state to TypeSafe. The host agent generates code, not Jev. Session limits use token estimates and usage accounting, not a guaranteed provider billing cap. Calibrate thresholds on separate labeled examples; listed performance and accuracy are not independently validated.

name: MinusPodJev
description: Podcast ad-detection adapter for MinusPod: Jev scores transcript segments and code assembles the ad spans.
notes: Discovered through shipwithjev.com. Proof-of-concept proxy, not an audio-generation model. Source review covered segment questions, typed response validation, cache/invalid-probability regression tests, and security documentation; none was executed here. Sends transcript text to TypeSafe and forwards the caller's bearer key. Keep the proxy on a trusted connection; deployment needs request-size/rate limits in addition to its concurrency guard. Chapter generation still requires a separate chat model. Respect the licenses of vendored compatibility code and evaluation material; benchmark results were not reproduced.

name: jev-claude-statusline
description: Claude Code hooks send task text, recent tool summaries, latest assistant message, and turn status to Jev (Score phase plus Noul done/waiting_on_user); answers are cached and shown as a progress segment on the Claude Code status line.
notes: Author submission. Requires a TypeSafe API key and paid Jev inference. Not official TypeSafe software. Bash activity intended for Jev uses tool descriptions, not raw command text. Source packaging of a working local setup; the hook and live inference were not executed in this catalog review. Closest cousin: valentynkit/jev-belay (Stop-hook completion check); this project estimates continuous status-line progress.

name: SemDecide
description: Unix CLI for Jev predicates, choices, scores, JSONL filtering, and CI-friendly exit codes.
notes: Validates Jev response shapes and keeps uncertainty/provider failures distinct. Input is sent to the configured Jev endpoint; custom SEMDECIDE_API_URL values can carry the API key, so use a trusted HTTPS endpoint. Source-reviewed, not executed here.

name: Winnow
description: Claude Code context filter where Jev scores tool-output blocks and low-relevance blocks stay recallable from a local cache.
notes: Keeps uncertain blocks and error output rather than pruning them. Tool output reaches the configured judge; optional summaries use a separate model, while hidden full text is cached locally for recall. Published calibration results are author-reported and were not reproduced here.

name: DocJev
description: Classifies documents and finds packet boundaries with Jev after local parsing or optional cloud OCR.
notes: LiteParse extraction is local; normalized page text is sent to Jev. Optional LlamaParse uploads document bytes for OCR. The repository separates OCR and decision timing and labels its saved measurements; they were not reproduced here.

name: Leanest
description: Test selector that can use Jev to judge which Playwright or Vitest files are safe enough to skip for a code change.
notes: Jev is optional; classifier.dev is the default and Laya is another provider. The policy fails open on uncertainty/provider failure and has deterministic always-run overrides. Diff and test source reach the selected judge; use trusted HTTPS for a custom TypeSafe base URL. Source-reviewed, not executed here.

name: AnyJev
description: Independent typed-decision readouts for open models, with option-order correction and per-question calibration. Not TypeSafe Jev weights.
notes: Source and synthetic head-test review, not execution or reproduced benchmarks. L0 is not calibrated; L1/L2 need task-specific labels, and L2 heads are model-specific. The letter readout supports up to 26 options. Local Transformers and configurable vLLM backends have different data boundaries: vLLM receives submitted state and any configured bearer key; use trusted loopback or HTTPS. Models and datasets retain separate licenses. See docs/WEB_SWEEP_2026-09-25.md.

name: jev-align
description: Improves Jev classifiers and scoring rubrics with human labels and GEPA-proposed definition changes.
notes: Experimental definition optimization, not weight training. Selected dataset fields reach the Jev provider; labeled examples and rationales also reach the separately configured reflection model. Optional capture retains inputs locally, and registry publishing shares labeled data publicly. Review proposed edits and evaluate on held-out data; training scores are not generalization evidence. Evaluator, optimizer and mock-test source inspected; no upstream code, registry login or model calls run. See docs/WEB_SWEEP_2026-09-25.md.

name: neo4jev
description: Explores Neo4j graphs with Jev edge choices and goal checks inside a bounded beam search.
notes: Graph exploration demo, not a complete query engine. Node/relationship properties, path context and optional schema/property samples reach TypeSafe. Candidate caps and truncated properties can hide useful paths; the supplied hash-vector lookup is a placeholder, not semantic embeddings. Use a read-only database account and data approved for hosted processing. Navigator, access-layer and fake-client test source inspected; no database connection, upstream tests or inference run. See docs/WEB_SWEEP_2026-09-25.md.

name: patdown
description: Semantic linter that turns Markdown rules into Jev checks and maps flagged evidence back to source lines.
notes: Jev is the default, swappable judge. Selected paths, file content or stdin reach the provider; filename exclusions are not secret redaction. Custom TYPESAFE_BASE_URL does not enforce HTTPS: keep source and real keys on trusted HTTPS endpoints. The service validates finite yes-probabilities and removes provider prose from errors; this is not a security scanner or authorization boundary. Evidence-location calls add requests. Source and mocked error tests inspected, not executed. See docs/WEB_SWEEP_2026-09-25.md.

name: Jev-Mem
description: Research agent-memory system where Jev organizes graph memories and guides retrieval; a separate model writes answers.
notes: Research prototype with explicit response validation and retrieval budgets. Observations/context reach Jev; synthesis, judging and optional hosted embeddings use another provider. Caches retain conversations, and some persistence uses pickle: load only trusted files. Custom TypeSafe endpoints need trusted HTTPS. The mock demo is not a quality test; published LoCoMo results were not reproduced, and reference-aware best-of selection can bias evaluation. Client/configuration/security and offline-test source inspected, not run. See docs/WEB_SWEEP_2026-09-25.md.

name: Supercov
description: Coverage, security, and code-quality checks where Jev evaluates source files while test coverage remains local.
notes: Jev provides advisory source-only quality and security judgments; source files reach TypeSafe when scoring, while coverage and test execution remain local. Custom TypeSafe endpoints require HTTPS except loopback HTTP. Security findings are not a security audit. Source, endpoint guards, tests, and documentation were inspected; no upstream project code, test suite, or paid inference was run here.

name: Open Medical Jev
description: Independent frozen-model medical decision router using two local Qwen readers, confidence fusion, a Chow gate, and conformal candidate sets.
notes: Independent Jev-class research system, not TypeSafe Jev weights and not a medical device. The frozen readers are served locally; the repository ships code and recipes but no model weights, exam corpora, or per-item restricted evaluation data. Default calibration constants are distribution-bound and require recalibration under shift. Reported medical-exam accuracy, calibration, latency, and comparison figures are author-reported and were not reproduced here. Source, protocol, calibration, data policy, tests, and current upstream CI were inspected; no models or third-party project code were executed.

name: Jev in the Wild
description: Data-driven survey of 2,170 public Jev projects, mapping early growth, application domains, and decision-use patterns.
notes: An arXiv software-engineering preprint about public Jev applications, not a runnable Jev integration or independent model evaluation.

name: Jev vs an LLM: the numbers builders published
description: Puts published Jev and LLM runs of the same job side by side and lists the cases where the larger model still won.
notes: Submitted by Jon Kraayenbrink, who runs madewithjev.com. A compilation of builder-reported numbers, not independent measurements or a runnable integration; part of the page is embedded builder posts.

name: 1 Million Emojis
description: Shared 1000 × 1000 emoji canvas where Jev chooses an emoji and nearby square, or judges whether code should finish a stroke.
notes: Submitted by cwdx in PR #22. Inspected the public canvas logic, Jev client and unit-test source; no tests or paid inference were run. The inspected request sends stroke geometry, nearby emoji names and a text grid, without painter identity. The client routes through Vercel AI Gateway with TypeSafe HTTPS as fallback; running inference from source requires an API key. The repository mirrors reusable packages, not the hosted site's server. Visitor limits and the daily spending cap are author-described and were not verified; no shared canvas was changed.

name: jevotron
description: CLI that uses Jev to flag anomalies in selected fields, with file-format adapters, local previews and cached assessments.
notes: Submitted by Chris Mungall in PR #25. Live scans send full parsed entries, guidance and exemplars to TypeSafe; selecting fields limits scoring, not the context transmitted. The local SQLite cache retains request and response text. Preview is offline; Python config files execute code and must be trusted. Client, request construction, response validation, cache, example and fake-client test source inspected; no upstream code, tests or paid inference executed. Author pilot results were not reproduced.

name: WaterSheep
description: Independent open-weight model for yes/no, choice, score and multi-label questions, with option probabilities. Not TypeSafe Jev weights.
notes: Submitted by Samrat Dutta in PR #26. The local CLI binds 127.0.0.1 and answers POST /v1/systemone without calling TypeSafe; model files are downloaded separately from Hugging Face. The project documents Python SDK routing through TYPESAFE_BASE_URL; compatibility was source-reviewed, not executed. English only, with truncated long inputs; large option sets use grouping and tournament passes. Calibration and accuracy are author-reported, domain-dependent and not reproduced. Model, inference, local server, request example, toy self-test, license and published model metadata inspected; no models or third-party code run.

name: TetraJev
description: Independent research recipes combining letter and per-option readouts from two frozen local models, with agreement-based decision routing.
notes: Submitted by Fei Liu in issue #21. Research scripts and aggregate results, not TypeSafe Jev weights or a packaged decision service. Local core inference uses separately obtained Qwen models through llama.cpp; --server is caller-configured, and the optional run_jev_api.py reference runner sends benchmark state to paid TypeSafe inference. Adapt hard-coded local paths before reuse. Author accuracy and coverage curves were not reproduced; retrospective coverage is not a deployment guarantee, and equal-weight fusion can underperform a stronger reader. Method, readouts, fusion/routing code, usage examples, data policy and license inspected; no project code or models run.

name: JevPDF
description: Highlights PDF lines that answer a natural-language query; pdf.js extracts text locally and Jev scores each candidate line.
notes: Original X post: 2026-09-23. Exact text search stays local; meaning search sends extracted page text and the query through the app server to TypeSafe. Optional user API keys also pass through that server. Text extraction is not OCR, and relevance scores do not establish factual correctness. Extraction/search/proxy source inspected; no PDF, key, paid call or benchmark used. Creator post is an indexed reference; X playback was not verified.

name: softlint
description: Checks changed diff hunks against plain-English rules, then asks Jev which added line best locates each finding.
notes: Original X post: 2026-09-20. Sends selected source diffs and rules to TypeSafe. Hunks are truncated to a fixed budget, so findings are limited to supplied context; this supplements code review and ordinary linting. The fake-shop example and injected-client test source were inspected. Advertised detection/cost results were not reproduced. Creator post is an indexed reference; X playback was not verified.

name: Jev Dreaming
description: Filters incoming text for memorable information and judges relationships between memories; Gemini generates the memory text.
notes: Original X post: 2026-09-23. Experimental memory-graph comparison with a Gemini-only pipeline, not validated memory accuracy. Text and candidate memories reach hosted providers; applying a run can update browser IndexedDB. The Jev route uses a server-held key without application authentication, so keep self-hosted exploration local. No public code license was verified; no project code or benchmarks were run. Creator post is an indexed reference; X playback was not verified.

name: ASIMOV Jev output filter
description: Filters fetched or listed JSON records with a plain-language Jev question before optional jq projection.
notes: Original X post: 2026-09-22; current source reviewed through 2026-10-07. --jev is optional and uses TYPESAFE_API_TOKEN. Original records reach TypeSafe before jq projection, so selecting fewer output fields does not reduce data sent upstream. Current filtering keeps scores strictly above 0.80, validates responses and surfaces failures. Implementation and regression-test source inspected; no modules, accounts or live calls used. Creator post is an indexed reference; X playback was not verified.

name: fast-jev-compaction
description: Experimental context pruning: Jev scores tool-call/result pairs, and local code keeps, truncates or drops them while preserving retained text.
notes: September 2026 creator post; the inspected mirror displays Sep 18, while the post ID encodes Sep 17 UTC. Conversation text and tool inputs reach TypeSafe, but tool-result bodies are omitted from the model's decision state. Pruning can discard useful evidence; the hook falls back to a normal summary on errors or insufficient reduction. The repository's animated demo is explicitly scripted; it is separate from the real API-backed library. Client, compaction, hook and fake-client test source inspected; no integration, quality/cost evaluation or paid inference run.

name: Jev dev
description: Desktop workbench for editing Jev requests, inspecting typed answers and keeping run history, with a separate demo mode.
notes: Live requests run in the desktop app with a TypeSafe API key; browser preview uses demo answers. Live inference sends the request state and questions to TypeSafe, and local run history retains request, response and error text. No code license was found in the reviewed source tree. Implementation, request example and test source inspected; no app, installer, project tests or inference run. Creator post is an indexed reference; X playback was not verified.

name: pi-jev-governor
description: Routes planning, model tier, tool permission and completion decisions for the pi coding agent, with deterministic gates and human or fail-closed fallbacks.
notes: Jev receives a scrubbed task prompt and bounded summaries for routing, permission and outcome judgments; sensitive tool inputs stay in a local confirmation or fail-closed path. The plugin is workflow control in the same process, not an OS sandbox. Remote outages fall back for routing and completion but keep the local permission gate active. Source, response validation, redaction, permission logic, test source and recorded local-mock acceptance evidence were inspected at the pinned revision; no dependency, project test, agent model or paid inference was run here.

name: pen-find
description: Finds Pen design frames by sending node names, paths, text and structure to Jev for semantic ranking.
notes: Reads a local Pen file through Pen's bundled MCP server and sends frame/group names, hierarchy paths, text, size and component/icon summaries to TypeSafe; do not use it for design text that must stay local. It stores its key and index cache owner-only and applies targeted secret-pattern redaction, which is not a guarantee that all sensitive design content is removed. Results are a shortlist for review, not verified matches. Implementation, install metadata, license and privacy documentation were inspected; no Pen file, skill installation, upstream code, paid inference or author speed/cost benchmark was run here.

name: Chirp
description: Turns coding-agent completion state into short synthesized notification sounds, with Jev choosing bounded mood and voice parameters.
notes: Sends up to roughly 900 characters from the beginning and end of an agent's last message, plus agent/project labels and timing, to TypeSafe. With no key or on API failure it uses a local punctuation/state fallback; sound synthesis and playback remain local. Treat the audio as an ambient notification, not a reliable task-success signal. Request construction, response parsing, synthesizer boundaries, test source, key handling and license were inspected; no plugin, Tern runtime, audio command, upstream tests or paid inference was run here.
